# dreamrouter_static_route (Resource)

A static route (Settings → Routing → Static Routes): traffic for network goes to next_hop, e.g. another router on your LAN with its own network behind it. The provider checks what the router doesn't: the next hop is a device on one of your networks (not the router itself) and the name is unique.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The network behind a second router on the LAN.
resource "dreamrouter_static_route" "cudy" {
  name     = "cudy"
  network  = "192.168.2.0/24"
  next_hop = "192.168.1.4"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the route, unique among static routes (case-insensitive).
- `network` (String) Destination network in network form, e.g. "192.168.2.0/24". Not one of the router's own networks, and not 0.0.0.0/0.
- `next_hop` (String) Address of the router to send the traffic to; a device on one of your networks.

### Optional

- `distance` (Number) Administrative distance, 1 to 255 (lower wins). Defaults to 1.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the route is active. Defaults to true.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The route's ID on the router.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a static route by its network (or name, or ID):
terraform import dreamrouter_static_route.cudy 192.168.2.0/24
```
